raw: 25.1 Typology: Terrorist, Criminal, Commercial, Hacktivist, Proxy[^12]
teaching_note: These are overlapping descriptors with different evidentiary and legal requirements, not mutually exclusive bins or a scale of guilt. Commercial activity or advocacy is not inherently hostile; 'proxy' requires a specified relationship, distinguishing support, alignment, tasking, direction and control. Code observed conduct separately from organizational self-description and contested labels [@ageint012].
title: Typology: Terrorist, Criminal, Commercial, Hacktivist, Proxy

raw: 25.2 Hezbollah, ISIS, MS-13: Intelligence Structures and Capabilities
teaching_note: These named organizations must not be treated as interchangeable in function, geography, period or legal status. The generic defensive references do not establish their intelligence structures or capabilities; require dated, organization-specific evidence and distinguish claims made by an actor from independently observed conduct. No capability or individual affiliation is inferred from the chapter list.
title: Hezbollah, ISIS, MS-13: bounded comparison and source gaps

raw: 25.3 Private Military Corporations as Intelligence Actors
teaching_note: A commercial contract, military-related service and intelligence role are separate facts; a contractor is not automatically a state proxy. Identify the contract period, stated service and independently evidenced conduct before considering sponsorship, leaving unknown direction/control explicit. Existing broad guidance does not support a current corporate roster or a general claim about all contractors.
title: Private Military Corporations as Intelligence Actors

teaching_note: Completed offline case: O1 is a synthetic organization's public claim to provide multilingual analysis; O2 is a supplied contract for translation; O3 is an aggregate funding table with an unexplained sponsor code; O4 repeats O1. The completed actor-conduct-source-date card records claimed analysis capability (O1), contracted translation only (O2), one dependent repeat (O4), and funding relationship unresolved (O3); neither effectiveness nor covert tasking follows. Withheld O5 decodes O3 as an ordinary publishing grant, so remove the asserted covert-funding inference while keeping any direction/control claim unsupported. Close that claim without real-person profiling; disagreement or shared rhetoric is not evidence of an operation (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]).
title: Counterintelligence Threat from Non-State Actors

raw: 25.5 Non-State Actor Use of Commercial AI for Intelligence Collection
teaching_note: Tool availability, claimed use, observed use and demonstrated operational effectiveness are four different propositions. STIX/TAXII describe representation and exchange, while ATLAS organizes AI-related threat knowledge; none establishes that a named organization used commercial AI or benefited from it. Preserve 'Non-State' and hold attribution when supplied artifacts cannot distinguish manual work, ordinary automation and model assistance.
title: Non-State Actor Use of Commercial AI for Intelligence Collection
